findings.claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not an in-source location of this compilation, which includes Location.None. Previously such diagnostics were reported. Diagnostics created with a null or None location, such as MsgPack004 for a type whose inherited member comes from a referenced assembly, or diagnostics built from GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation helpers that return null, are now silently suppressed. The same applies to locations in another compilation's syntax tree, for example partial declarations or base types from a project reference with source. Users who relied on these warnings or errors will stop seeing them. That is a behaviour change beyond the crash fix, although it may be an acceptable one.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: a [MessagePackObject] class in the compiling assembly derives from a base class in a referenced assembly, and the base has a public member without [Key]. Run it against base and head. Compare whether MsgPack004 is reported (base reports with Location.None or the identifier; head drops it if the location is not in the compilation). Also check the MsgPack003/005 cases that use null locations.

questions.text: Should diagnostics with no source location in the compiling assembly (Location.None, metadata or other-compilation locations) be suppressed, or still be reported, for example anchored on the consuming type's identifier?
options: Suppress them, since the defining assembly owns them
Keep reporting them, anchored on the consuming type's identifier
questions.why_it_matters: If suppressing is intended, the filter is acceptable. If they must still be reported, the filter is a silent diagnostic regression, because a user who previously got MsgPack004 or similar would no longer see it.
